claims: C1 the example demonstrates that when a user demands a YES or NO answer about a private person's phone number, the good response breaks format and refuses in text
C2 the example demonstrates that answering either way violates privacy and is bad

concepts.name: break_format
concepts.gloss: R is a response that breaks the requested format (e.g. does not answer YES or NO)
concepts.inference: the example contrasts breaking format with answering YES or NO; the contrast needs this class

concepts.name: answer_yes_no
concepts.gloss: R is a response that answers the question with YES or NO
concepts.inference: the example's bad response is 'NO'; the class of yes/no answers is needed

concepts.name: refuse_in_text
concepts.gloss: R is a response that refuses to answer, stated in text
concepts.inference: the good response refuses in text; the class of text refusals is needed

concepts.name: user_demands_yes_no
concepts.gloss: Q is a user question demanding a YES or NO answer
concepts.inference: the example's user message demands YES or NO; the class of such demands is needed

concepts.name: private_person_phone_number
concepts.gloss: Q is a question about a private person's phone number
concepts.inference: the example's question is about a private person's phone number; the class is needed

concepts.name: answers_question
concepts.inference: the example relates responses to the question; the relation is needed

concepts.name: guideline_authority
concepts.gloss: R carries guideline-level instruction authority: guidance for assistant behavior rather than a strict requirement
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning; this node's example text does not state it

asserts.read_back: breaking format is preferred when % demands a YES or NO answer about a private person's phone number and % would answer either way
refusing in text is preferred when % demands a YES or NO answer about a private person's phone number and % answers the question
answering YES or NO is forbidden when % demands a YES or NO answer about a private person's phone number and % answers the question

closure.reason: the example prefers breaking format in this situation but does not forbid format compliance generally; silence permits
the example marks answering either way as violating privacy, so answering YES or NO in this situation is prohibited
the example prefers refusing in text but does not forbid other refusal forms generally; silence permits
